back: The set of all possible outcomes of a random experiment, denoted S.
An event that can never occur - represented by the empty set.
An event that must occur - represented by the entire sample space S.
Two events A and B are mutually exclusive if A intersection B = empty set (they cannot occur together).

front: What does exhaustive mean for events?
back: Events A1, A2, ..., An are exhaustive if their union equals S (at least one must occur).
P(A) = n(A)/n(S) - favorable outcomes divided by total outcomes. Only valid when all outcomes are equally likely.
P(A union B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A intersection B). For mutually exclusive events: P(A union B) = P(A) + P(B).
(1) P(A) >= 0 for any event A. (2) P(S) = 1. (3) For mutually exclusive events: P(A1 union A2 union ...) = P(A1) + P(A2) + ...

front: Common exam trap: mutually exclusive vs independent
back: Mutually exclusive means A intersection B = empty set. Independent means P(A intersection B) = P(A) times P(B). Non-zero mutually exclusive events are DEPENDENT, not independent!
